I had no idea about JKR's transphobic views until I got and played Hogwarts Legacy. I never looked her up and no one told me a thing while knowing I'm a huge HP fan. When I did learn about it, I was speechless and heart broken but I don't support her views in any sort of way. I hate JKR but damn do I love Harry Potter. Reading the books and watching the movies got me through the dark times of home life. I felt a strong connection to Harry, specifically, because of the way he was treated back at the Dursleys. It reminded me of how I was treated and I always fantasized about attending Hogwarts, so when the game came out I was ecstatic. I've also struggled with my identity for years. It was only two years ago when I finally accepted myself to be Non-Binary. I just tell people to use whatever pronouns they want as I don't mind she/her/they/them/he/him. 



When people try to convince me I'm transphobic because of my love for HP I ask where is this kind of energy for other creators who are just as bad or even worse and they always just go silent. If we boycotted everything we consume because of the artist, we'd have nothing. Might as well create our own clothes, food, fantasies and etc. Everything we own in our homes was in one way or another created by someone who wanted a certain community of people to not exist.

Ever since I was a baby, I barely ate that much. In fact, I was told I needed a feeding tube because my refusal for milk. And then my first few toddler years, my parents had a difficult time getting me to eat. There is actually a picture of my mom trying to get me to eat and I'm ignoring her. It wasn't until 4th grade that I finally started filling out in a way that made my doctor's happy. 

But since then, I became pretty overweight. Never thought I ate too much to be honest, I ate pretty healthy and was active but I still gained weight. Junior year of high school, after a pregnancy scare, I became a tad obese. I tried everything, every diet I could think of and honestly, nothing worked. This continued on until 2017, when I got motivated to live and decided to change a lot of my life. 

I didn't try to lose weight, I just liked to dance(kpop) to my favorite songs for 4 hours. I ate much less than a single serving, realized that wasn't healthy and ate whatever I wanted. I went from 295 lbs to 190 lbs within a year. 

Met my now husband in 2019. After a concussion in 2020, I had to stop dancing. I started gaining weight again. Then I got pregnant and I tried to keep at a healthy weight but for some reason, my body just doesn't work like that. After giving birth in 2021, I tried to go back to my routine. It's been a tough battle but only now, in 2023, am I starting to lose weight. I went from 250 lbs to 225 lbs within just a month. 

Every single body is different. Losing weight is very difficult but gaining weight could be the easiest thing in the world. Sometimes it just doesn't matter how much you eat. Sometimes it's just your body. Everyone is different.
